message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time)**  
- Standard Time (PST): UTC‑8  
- Daylight Saving Time (PDT): UTC‑7  

**Berlin (Central European Time)**  
- Standard Time (CET): UTC +1  
- Daylight Saving Time (CEST): UTC +2  

Because both cities observe daylight‑saving time but **start and end it on different dates**, the time difference can vary:

| Period | Berlin | Los Angeles | Difference |
|--------|--------|-------------|------------|
| **Standard Time** (both on standard) | UTC +1 | UTC‑8 | **9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| **Daylight Saving Time** (both on DST) | UTC +2 | UTC‑7 | **9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| **Transition windows** (when one city is on DST and the other isn’t) | | | **10 hours** (Berlin is 10 h ahead) |

### Transition windows

| Date range (approx.) | Which city has switched? | Difference |
|----------------------|--------------------------|------------|
| Early March – mid‑March | Berlin switches to CEST before LA switches to PDT | 10 h |
| Late October – early November | Berlin switches back to CET before LA switches back to PST | 10 h |

So, outside those transition windows, Berlin is consistently **9 hours ahead** of Los Angeles. During the brief periods when only one city is observing DST, the difference expands to **10 hours**.
